findings.reason: §16's node should name the existing stranded-launch owner (and its reflex caller at dispatch_review_for_run, recovery.py:2374-2387) and either move the plan-review pointer write after admission or release through `_discard_stranded_review`, so one classifier decides "never launched" instead of a second path for plan-review runs alone.
findings.text: §16 states its defect as "the plan-review path through `dispatch_review_for_run` keeps a claim that a refused or abandoned launch should release" and proposes new machinery to release it, without citing `_stranded_launch`, which already returns True for exactly §16's pointer: phase `starting` (in `_PRE_SPAWN_PHASES`, recovery.py:6245), no pid, no worker record, no stream, no launch log, started past the 900 s bound — the §16 example sat 49 minutes

findings.reason: naming the owner lets the fix land once, at the pre-admission pointer write, rather than forking the release and re-deriving the same bound for the plan-review lane.
findings.text: the release §16 describes would be a second "release a launch that never spawned" path beside `_discard_stranded_review`, which the reflex already calls; the recovery module already owns detection (`_stranded_launch`) and release (`_discard_stranded_review`) of a pre-spawn pointer

findings.reason: the landing already extended this exact owner (merge 1be48d1ff, recorded in the plan's own §11 comments), so the design was right and only the body is stale; the plan should mark §11 landed by pointer to that comment rather than re-open it.
findings.text: §11's body proposes a launch-time "held session" detector and a stderr-reading observe without citing `member_in_flight_verdict`/`refuse_member_in_flight`, whose docstring already states §11's defect almost verbatim: "a dispatch launches onto a member whose session still has a live writer, where the backend's single-writer store then kills the launch before its first turn"

findings.reason: the plan already records the destination decision and the transitional inert state behind `RECKON_FLEET_SPAWN`, so naming the retirement would not change the design; it is a follow-on for the dotfiles half.
findings.text: the §10 batch step is now implemented twice: the reader carried into reckon (`fleet_supervisor.py`, verb `spawn`) and dotfiles' `bin/fleet-supervisor`, which the §10 landing records as "unmodified, and so is every caller"; the §10 fleet-supervisor node names the lead's decision to move it into reckon but the plan never names dotfiles' copy as the owner to retire

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the per-run supervisor (§3) and the fleet batch step (§10) keep one launch behaviour behind a small interface: one shared argv vector (`_supervisor_argv`, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:9571), a serialized spec, and an acknowledgement file, so the batch step stays free of reckon knowledge rather than a spread of type-one wrappers. `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` (1355 lines) is a genuinely deep module hiding the FIFO loop, runtime directory and spawn handshake.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16's plan-review pointer release duplicates the stranded-launch release owned by `reckon/crew/recovery.py` (`_stranded_launch` :6585, `_discard_stranded_review` :1314), and the batch-step protocol is carried twice (reckon `fleet_supervisor.py` beside dotfiles' `bin/fleet-supervisor`).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the landed sections cite and extend their owners, but §16 proposes releasing an abandoned plan-review pointer without citing `_stranded_launch` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:6585) and `_discard_stranded_review` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:1314), which already detect and release exactly that shape.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §11's hold-or-divert extends `member_in_flight_verdict`/`refuse_member_in_flight` (reckon/crew/node.py:357, :391) and observe's `launch-failed` arm (reckon/crew/recovery.py:8764) rather than layering a second detector over them; the landed merge 1be48d1ff confirmed this. The section body is stale (still `implementable`) but the design is the right shape.
